untertitel: Wishes and plans with *would like to* – write a message and reply

grammatik.regel: _would like_ + *to* + base verb says what you want to do: I _would like_ *to bring* a cake. In short: I'd like to … In questions, _Would_ comes first: _Would_ you _like_ *to play* football? Without a second verb it also works: I'd like a coffee. Use a with one thing (a cake), an before a vowel sound (an apple), some with food and drink or plurals (some bread).

redemittel.p2: I'd like to bring some bread and cheese.
Yes, please! / No, I'd rather listen to music.

soGehts: You and your partner are planning a picnic in the park on Sunday.
Cut page 2 in half. Partner A takes the left half, Partner B the right half.
On your own: Put the words in order and write two sentences with would like to.
On your own: Write your partner a message (part 1). The words in the box help you.
Swap sheets. Read the message and reply (part 2). At the end, read both messages aloud.

hinweise: Say what you would like to bring: a cake, an apple, some juice.
After would like, use to + the base verb (to bring, to play).

loesungen.antwort: I would like to bring a cake.

I would like to bring a blanket.

Message A, for example: Hi Sam, we're having a picnic in the park on Sunday! I would like to bring a cake and some apple juice. Would you like to play football? I would like to come at 2 pm. Best wishes, Lea

Message B, for example: Hi Lea, I'm looking forward to Sunday! I would like to bring a blanket and some bread and cheese. We would like to sit by the lake, it's lovely there. Would you like to listen to music? See you on Sunday, Sam
